knowledge:
- key_parameters: threshSig=Threshold for calling significant tests to estimate parameters (e.g., 0.05) ;; threshNull=Threshold for calling null tests to estimate parameters (e.g., 0.5) ;; n=Allowed fraction of non-missing data across states to keep a QTL association (e.g., 0.5) ;; thresh=Primary threshold for calling significance ;; secondThresh=Secondary threshold for a flexible two-step significance calling approach ;; mode=Mode of significance calling (e.g., "simple") ;; annotateColsBy=Column metadata names from colData to annotate plots ;; annotateRowsBy=Row metadata names from rowData to annotate plots
- alternatives: mashr=Multi-test correction method wrapper ;; meta-soft=Multi-test correction method wrapper ;; sumstats2qtle=Function from QTLExperiment package used to read in real QTL summary statistics instead of simulating them
- when_to_use: When analyzing QTL summary statistics (betas, standard errors, p-values, or lfsrs) across multiple states (such as different tissues, cell types, or environmental conditions) to identify shared, multi-state, or state-specific QTLs.
- pitfalls: vroom does not read .gz compressed objects well, which can truncate loaded results if not handled properly ;; Using a single strict threshold for calling significance across states can result in low recall of true significant QTLs; a flexible two-step threshold approach (thresh and secondThresh) is recommended to improve performance ;; Missing data (NAs) in assays can affect downstream analyses, requiring filtering with getComplete and imputation with replaceNAs before running certain metrics.

workflows.name: multistate_qtl_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze, preprocess, call significance, and visualize multi-state QTL summary statistics across different tissues or conditions.
input: input_df (A data frame containing state names and file paths to QTL summary statistics files)
qtl_summary_stats.tsv (Tab-separated files containing molecular trait IDs, variant IDs, betas, standard errors, and p-values for each state)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and format QTL summary statistics into a QTLExperiment object using sumstats2qtle ;; 2. Estimate simulation parameters from the input data using qtleEstimate ;; 3. Simulate multi-state QTL data using qtleSimulate ;; 4. Filter out associations with high missingness using getComplete ;; 5. Impute remaining missing values using replaceNAs ;; 6. Call significance across states using single or two-step thresholds with callSignificance ;; 7. Evaluate significance calling performance using simPerformance ;; 8. Calculate pairwise sharing and identify top hits using getSignificant, getTopHits, and runPairwiseSharing ;; 9. Visualize global sharing patterns using plotPairwiseSharing and plotUpSet ;; 10. Categorize QTLs into global, multi-state, or unique types using runTestMetrics and visualize with plotCompareStates and plotQTLClusters
workflows.code:
library(QTLExperiment)
library(multistateQTL)

input_path <- system.file("extdata", package="multistateQTL")
state <- c("lung", "thyroid", "spleen", "blood")

input <- data.frame(
    state=state, 
    path=paste0(input_path, "/GTEx_tx_", state, ".tsv"))

gtex <- sumstats2qtle(
    input, 
    feature_id="molecular_trait_id",
    variant_id="rsid", 
    betas="beta", 
    errors="se",
    pvalues="pvalue", 
    verbose=TRUE)

params <- qtleEstimate(gtex, threshSig=0.05, threshNull=0.5)

plotSimulationParams(params=params)

sim <- qtleSimulate(
    nStates=10, nFeatures=100, nTests=1000,
    global=0.2, multi=0.4, unique=0.2, k=2)

sim_na <- sim
na_pattern <- sample(seq(1, ncol(sim)*nrow(sim)), 1000)
assay(sim_na, "betas")[na_pattern] <- NA
assay(sim_na, "errors")[na_pattern] <- NA
assay(sim_na, "lfsrs")[na_pattern] <- NA

sim_na <- getComplete(sim_na, n=0.5, verbose=TRUE)

sim_na <- replaceNAs(sim_na, verbose=TRUE)

sim <- callSignificance(
    sim, mode="simple", assay="lfsrs",
    thresh=0.0001, secondThresh=0.0002)

perf_metrics <- simPerformance(sim)

sim_sig <- getSignificant(sim)
sim_top <- getTopHits(sim_sig, assay="lfsrs", mode="state")
sim_top <- runPairwiseSharing(sim_top)
p1 <- plotPairwiseSharing(sim_top, annotateColsBy=c("nSignificant", "multistateGroup"))

plotUpSet(sim_top, annotateColsBy=c("nSignificant", "multistateGroup"))

sim_top <- runTestMetrics(sim_top)

plotCompareStates(sim_top, x="S01", y="S02")

sim_top_ms <- subset(sim_top, qtl_type_simple == "multistate")

plotQTLClusters(
    sim_top_ms, 
    annotateColsBy=c("multistateGroup"),
    annotateRowsBy=c("qtl_type", "mean_beta", "QTL"))
